A previous import collapsed the invoice, inventory and reporting logic into a single catch-all package under internal/legacy (internal/legacy/legacy.go), with the unrelated concerns sharing terse internal names and a barrel file (internal/legacy/barrel.go) re-exposing them under their original public spellings. The service code has become hard to maintain and extend since that import.

Reorganize this logic into two clear, single-responsibility packages at the canonical layout the rest of the codebase expects:
- internal/service/invoices.go (package service): the invoice-creation logic together with the inventory/stock logic it depends on, exporting the public constructors NewInvoiceService and NewInventoryService and their types and errors.
- internal/reports/reports.go (package reports): the tenant revenue reporting and the by-status summary, exporting the public constructor NewService and its types.

The HTTP handlers under internal/handlers and the cmd/bizflowd entry point currently import internal/legacy; rewire them onto the new internal/service and internal/reports packages. The observable behavior and the public API must not change. Delete internal/legacy once nothing depends on it.
issue_title: Service code is hard to maintain after a legacy import
issue_body:
A previous import collapsed the invoice, inventory and reporting logic into a single catch-all package under internal/legacy (internal/legacy/legacy.go), with the unrelated concerns sharing terse internal names and a barrel file (internal/legacy/barrel.go) re-exposing them under their original public spellings. The service code has become hard to maintain and extend since that import.

Reorganize this logic into two clear, single-responsibility packages at the canonical layout the rest of the codebase expects:
- internal/service/invoices.go (package service): the invoice-creation logic together with the inventory/stock logic it depends on, exporting the public constructors NewInvoiceService and NewInventoryService and their types and errors.
- internal/reports/reports.go (package reports): the tenant revenue reporting and the by-status summary, exporting the public constructor NewService and its types.

The HTTP handlers under internal/handlers and the cmd/bizflowd entry point currently import internal/legacy; rewire them onto the new internal/service and internal/reports packages. The observable behavior and the public API must not change. Delete internal/legacy once nothing depends on it.
expected_behavior: Invoice creation, inventory reservation and tenant revenue reporting all produce the same results as before.
The invoice and inventory logic is reachable through the internal/service package and the reporting logic through the internal/reports package, under their public names.
The HTTP handlers continue to construct and serve the same services, and the catch-all package is gone.
Each concern lives in its own focused package.
expected_failure_summary: Invoice/inventory/reporting concerns are collapsed into the opaque internal/legacy package under terse names with a re-export barrel; the canonical internal/service and internal/reports packages do not exist, so behaviour cannot be imported at its expected location and a build against the canonical packages fails.
task_author_notes: Broken collapses the invoice+inventory+reporting logic into a single internal/legacy/legacy.go under terse names (Iv/Iw/Rp, A/R/C/Mk/Rv/S) plus internal/legacy/barrel.go aliasing those onto the public spellings (InvoiceService/InventoryService/ReportService, Create/Reserve/Available/TenantReport/StatusSummary). Handlers and cmd are wired through internal/legacy. A correct reorg relocates the logic into just two canonical files: internal/service/invoices.go (package service, holding both the invoice and inventory logic, exporting NewInvoiceService/NewInventoryService and the Err* values) and internal/reports/reports.go (package reports, exporting NewService), then rewires internal/handlers/{invoices,reports}.go and cmd/bizflowd/main.go onto them, and deletes internal/legacy. The hidden check.go imports bizflow/internal/service and bizflow/internal/reports directly: on broken those two packages are absent so it fails to compile; on gold it compiles and the behavioural assertions pass. The visible test imports only the stable internal/bizdb + internal/repository + internal/store seam (unchanged by the reorg) so it runs on both snapshots. internal/store, internal/repository, internal/model, internal/apiutil, internal/bizdb, migrations are unchanged between gold and broken.
